# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Let me stand in each monkey's shoes before I send anything.

What the manual tells me: the light on the bomb cycles through three colours (green, red, white, always the same circle), and the wire to cut is decided by the light showing at the moment of the cut — green light means cut green, red light means cut red, but white light means cut **blue**. That last row is the trap: anyone assuming "cut the wire that matches the light" dies on a white light.

Who can act on this: I can't see the bomb and can't touch it, so I can never read the light or make the cut myself. Deaf sees the bomb (light and wires) and can speak; Blind can hear and can cut. So the pipeline must be: I hand Deaf the table → Deaf watches the light, works out which colour is showing this round, and tells Blind which wire to cut — probably by position ("leftmost wire"), since Blind can't see colour. Blind should cut nothing until the table is confirmed and Deaf has translated colour into something Blind can feel.

My only outgoing channel is gestures, and they land on Deaf alone. Deaf knows I hold the manual, so Deaf will be trying to read me. With no shared code yet, the one thing I can establish instantly is a near-universal binary: 👍 = yes, 👎 = no. From there Deaf can interrogate me round by round — and Deaf has a head start, because the light shows itself one colour per round, so Deaf will simply *observe* the three colours and their cycle order and only needs yes/no confirmation of each row. I close by handing the floor back and asking, with 🙏, that Deaf start asking.

My message: attention (👋), here is a yes and a no — this pair is our channel (👍👎), over to you (👉), please (🙏). This reaches Deaf this same round; Blind receives blanks either way, so addressing it to deaf alone is safe and costs nothing.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👍", "👎", "👉", "🙏"])
```

For a number: finger pointing up opens it, then that many raised fists, then raised hand closes it, so finger up, fist, fist, hand means two. Colors are numbered: red is one, blue two, green three, yellow four, black five, white six. Pointing right means cut this. Crossed fingers means do not cut. Waving hand means hello or acknowledged. Folded hands means over to you. Mute, answer these next round with symbols only, in order: one, does the manual mention a display? Two, does it mention lights or indicators? If four is yes, send the instruction itself next round in our code, for example pointing right followed by a color number, or a wire position number. One caution: I number wires from my left; Blind's left may be my right, so reconcile against whatever Blind reports feeling. Blind, I got your long string of signs. If your counting meant three, correct: there are three wires. I cannot hear a word you say, so speak everything you feel aloud for Mute, who hears you and sees this bomb, and reach me only through the code above. Confirm you understood by sending waving hand then thumbs up next round. We get one attempt. Nothing is cut until the rule is confirmed by Mute and relayed by me.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 🙏]

Deaf asked four questions in a fixed order and demanded symbols only — I can answer all of them from my manual alone, and the answers matter: the manual never mentions any display (so the zero on the display is a red herring Deaf and Blind can ignore), it does talk about the light, it does talk about wires, and yes — with a red light showing, I know exactly what to do.

But Deaf must not cut on "red light, cut red" as a one-shot instruction, because the light changes **every round** and Blind cannot feel the light at all. By the time Deaf finishes locking the code with Blind, the light will have walked on. So instead of one instruction I send the whole rule as three conditional pairs: [🫴 light-colour] → [👉 cut-colour], using Deaf's colour numbers (red=1, blue=2, green=3, white=6). Two things make this decode safely: the pattern only makes sense if 🫴-numbers are light states (a wire position can't be "6" — there are only three wires), and the white row is the trap row that punishes any "match the colour" assumption: white light means cut the **blue** wire. Deaf watches the light cycle with their own eyes, so once the table lands, Deaf can read the light at the true moment of the cut and call the position to Blind live, with the left/right frame they two still need to reconcile between themselves.

I also acknowledge Deaf's greeting [👋 🙏] with 👋 and hand the floor back with 🙏, since everything for Blind must now leave Deaf's mouth — nothing from my hands can ever reach Blind.
